pr_body:
This replaces direct `document.getElementsByName` lookups with a helper method which:
 - Lets the AnnotationLayer use the data returned by the `PDFDocumentProxy.getFieldObjects` API-method, such that we can directly lookup only the necessary DOM elements.
 - Fallback to using `document.getElementsByName` as before, such that e.g. the standalone viewer components still work.

Finally, to fix the problems reported in issue 14003, regardless of the code-path we now also enforce that the DOM elements found were actually created by the AnnotationLayer code.
With these changes we'll thus be able to update form elements on all visible pages just as before, but we'll additionally update the AnnotationStorage for not-yet-rendered elements thus fixing a pre-existing bug.

Fixes #14003

issue_context.title: Hazard: annotation_layer.js uses document.getElementsByName without verification
issue_context.body:
`annotation_layer.js` has logic to keep input elements in sync. The logic uses `document.getElementsByName` with [a name derived from the PDF](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/10a1db698047e612e8ae3da66d12a6c1ac5597a3/src/core/annotation.js#L407) to retrieve the set of related elements. This query is not namespaced, so if the viewer ever adds a `name` attribute to a checkbox or radio input in the page, then the PDF file can get it changed (without user interaction via the scripting interface). Fortunately, there doesn't appear to be any input/radio element in the default viewer code. A custom viewer can be affected by this bug, however.

I suggest to replace the `document.getElementsByTagName` calls with a function that checks that the elements are created by the `annotation_layer.js` code before returning them. There are several ways to do so, e.g. by adding a custom attribute to each input element.

## Seemingly generic property assignment
This code on its own looks dangerous because it allows the caller to overwrite any property
https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/99e442941c16561e8826a925b164d79f4ad51fbf/src/display/annotation_layer.js#L684-L688
Fortunately, it is only called with a fixed key, so only the `value` property can be updated in response to user input events:
https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/99e442941c16561e8826a925b164d79f4ad51fbf/src/display/annotation_layer.js#L732-L740

## Unchecking other checkboxes on checkbox state change
https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/99e442941c16561e8826a925b164d79f4ad51fbf/src/display/annotation_layer.js#L979-L990

## Updating the abstract state (storage)
https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/99e442941c16561e8826a925b164d79f4ad51fbf/src/display/annotation_layer.js#L1061-L1065

## Allowing scripts to uncheck checkbox/radio inputs
The others require user interaction to have any effect; this one allows scripts embedded in the PDF to run logic without user interaction.
https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/99e442941c16561e8826a925b164d79f4ad51fbf/src/display/annotation_layer.js#L1073-L1077

review_comments:
Could the `name` assignment be moved from below to this location, so that it is more obvious to which name this element is associated? That would also be more consistent with the other 3 initializations of `GetElementsByNameSet`.
https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/6040ae32819c454d8e1724c9d298e94b64e76f67/src/display/annotation_layer.js#L954

As mentioned in https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/pull/14023#issue-995915957, that's to ensure that the standalone viewer components won't break.
See https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/tree/master/examples/components, and in particular the `pageviewer` example, which uses a simplified AnnotationLayer-initialization without all of the parameters that the default viewer will provide.

nit: I think that it'd be slightly better to have a `Map` `name => [ids....]` generated from `parameters.fieldObjects` where fields with `page === -1` are removed this way we don't have to check in `_getElementsByName`. Since we needn't other properties than id, it should help to slightly reduce memory use.

> [...] with `page === -1` are removed this way we don't have to check in `_getElementsByName`.

You're correct that this would slightly reduce the necessary parsing here, however...

> it should help to slightly reduce memory use.

That would actually *increase* overall memory usage, since it'd force us to allocate one `Map` per page whereas currently every page simply gets *the same* Object (since the API implements caching).

I'd imagine a pdf with on page 1: a text field, a radio and a checkbox and the same on page 2 and page 4 (or more if needed) with the same fields with the same name.
Fill elements on page 1 then scroll on page 2, check that the values are correct (they should have been updated thanks to document.get...) and the same with page 4 (updated through annotationStorage).

The line here:

open the given pdf and the form is ready when the element with the given id is displayed.
and here you've a way to scroll to the page 4:
https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/master/test/integration/scripting_spec.js#L770
Maybe we could create the simplified fieldObjects before to pass it to the layer.
@Snuffleupagus, if you don't have time to write a test or don't feel like to do it, tell me and I'll write it later today or tomorrow.

> Maybe we could create the simplified fieldObjects before to pass it to the layer.

We could, but I don't want to do that for two reasons:
 - It would make the viewer components more difficult to use standalone, since it'd then not be enough just to call the correct API-method but you'd also need to *manually* transform the data into the required format.
 - It's not inconceivable that we'll want to add some other (future) `fieldObjects` usage in the AnnotationLayer, and if so we'd then need yet *another* external transformation or a breaking change of e.g. the `DefaultAnnotationLayerFactory` class.

All-in-all, I'm going to leave this as-is since the very slight overhead during parsing still ought to be lower than having to use `document.getElementsByName` unconditionally as in the current code.
